body.translated_text: <s>Vinayaviniścaya</s> — <s>Upāliparipṛcchā</s> (The Inquiry of <s>Upāli</s> Regarding the Determination of Vinaya)

body.text: namo buddhāya // tena khalu punaḥ samayenāyuṣmānupaliḥ pratisaṃlayanāta vyutthāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtyaikāntaṃ nyasīdat / ekānta niṣaṇnaścāyuṣmānupāliḥ bhagavantametadavocat / iha bhagavanmamaikākino rahogatasya pratisaṃlīna cittasyāyamevaṃrupaścetasi cetaḥparivitarka udapādi / prātimokṣasaṃvaro bhagavatā prajñaptaścādhiśīlaśikṣā pariśuddhiḥ śrāvakayānikānāṃ pratyekabuddhayānikānām ca / bodhisatvāyānikānāṃ tu bhagavatā jīvitaparityāge 'pi śikṣāpyatra parideśitā nirdiṣṭā / tat kathaṃ bhagavataḥ parinirvṛtasya tiṣṭhato vā śrāvakayānikānāṃ prātimokṣasaṃvaro vaktavyaḥ / kathaṃ pratyekabuddhayānikānām / kathaṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ prātimokṣasaṃvaro vaktavyaḥ / ahaṃ bhagavatā vinayaparāṇāmagro nirddiṣṭaḥ / tasya me bhagavan vijñāpayatūpāyakauśalyaṃ samprakāśayatu bhagavan yathā bhagavataḥ sakāśāt sammukhaṃ śrutvā sammukhaṃ pratigṛhya vaiśāradyaprāptaḥ parṣatsu vistareṇa saṃprakāśayeyam / ayaṃ me bhagavannekākino rahogatasya pratisaṃlīnasyaivaṃrupaścetasi cetaḥ parivitarka udapādi yattvahaṃ bhagavantamusaṃkramya vinayaviniścayaṃ paripṛccheyamiti / tat sādhu bhagavan vyākarotu tathāgato vinayaviniścayaṃ vistareṇa mahatī bhikṣuparṣata sannipatitā bodhisattvaparṣacca /
body.translated_text: Homage to the Buddha. Now at that time, the venerable <s>Upāli</s>, having risen from seclusion (<s>pratisaṃlayana</s>), approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he reverently saluted the feet of the Blessed One with his head, circumambulated three times, and sat down to one side. Having sat to one side, the venerable <s>Upāli</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: "Here, Blessed One, while I was alone, in seclusion, with my mind composed in meditation, a reflection of the following kind arose in my mind: The <s>prātimokṣasaṃvara</s> (restraint according to the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>) has been proclaimed by the Blessed One as the training in higher morality and purification for those following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Vehicle of Disciples) and those following the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> (Vehicle of Private Buddhas); but for those following the <s>Bodhisattvayāna</s> (Vehicle of Bodhisattvas), the Blessed One has taught and indicated a training even in the relinquishment of life itself. So how, when the Blessed One has passed into final <s>nirvāṇa</s> or while still present, should the <s>prātimokṣasaṃvara</s> be spoken of for those following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>? How for those following the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>? How should the <s>prātimokṣasaṃvara</s> be spoken of for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>? I have been designated by the Blessed One as foremost among those well-versed in the <s>Vinaya</s>. Therefore, Blessed One, please inform me of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), please illuminate [this matter], Blessed One — so that having heard face to face in the presence of the Blessed One and having received [the teaching] face to face, [I], having attained confidence (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), might expound it extensively in the assemblies. This, Blessed One, is the reflection that arose in my mind while I was alone, in seclusion, with my mind composed — that I should approach the Blessed One and inquire about the determination of the Vinaya (<s>vinayaviniścaya</s>). May the Blessed One graciously resolve [this matter] — may the <s>Tathāgata</s> explain the <s>vinayaviniścaya</s> in extenso; a great assembly of monks has gathered, and also an assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>."

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamupālimetadavocat / tasmāttarhitvamupāle anyena prayogeṇānyenādhyāśayena śrāvakayānikānāṃ śikṣāpariśuddhiṃ vada / anyena prayogeṇānyenādhyāśayena mahāyānasampratiṣṭhitānāṃ śikṣāpariśuddhiṃ vada / tat kasmāddhetoḥ / anyo hyupāle śrāvakayānikānāṃ prayogo 'nyo 'dhyāśayaḥ / anyo mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ prayogo 'nyo 'dhyāśayaḥ / tatropāleyā śrāvakayānikasya pariśuddhaśīlatā sā mahāyānikasya bodhisattvasyāpariśuddhaśīlatā paramadauḥśīlyañca / yā mahāyānasamprasthitasya bodhisattvasya pariśuddhaśīlatā sā śrāvakayānikasyāpariśuddhaśīlatā paramadauḥśīlyañca / tat kasmāddhetoḥ / ihopāle śrāvakayānikastatkṣaṇikacitte 'pi bhavopapattiṃ na parigṛṇhāti / iyaṃ śrāvakayānikasya pariśuddhaśīlatā sā mahāyānikasya bodhisatvasyā pariśuddhaśīlata paramadauḥ śīlyañca / katamopāle mahāyānasamprasthitasya bodhisattvasya pariśuddhaśīlatā yā śrāvakayānikasyāpariśuddhaśīlatā paramadauḥśilyañca / ihopāle mahāyāne samprasthito bodhisattvo 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyān kalpān bhavopapattiṃ parigṛṇhāti aparikhinnacitto 'parikhinnamānasaḥ / iyaṃ mahāyānasamprasthitasya bodhisattvasya pariśuddhaśīlatā sā śrāvakayānikasyāpariśuddhaśīlatā paramadauḥśīlyañca /
body.translated_text: Upon this being said, the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Upāli</s> thus: "Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, speak of the purification of training (<s>śikṣāpariśuddhi</s>) for those following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> with one [kind of] practice (<s>prayoga</s>) and one [kind of] resolve (<s>adhyāśaya</s>); speak of the purification of training for those established in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> with another practice and another resolve. For what reason? Because, <s>Upāli</s>, the practice of those following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> is one thing, their resolve is one thing; the practice of those who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is another thing, their resolve is another thing. Among these, <s>Upāli</s>: that which is pure morality (<s>pariśuddhaśīlatā</s>) for one following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> — that same [conduct] is impure morality (<s>apariśuddhaśīlatā</s>) and the height of immorality (<s>paramadauḥśīlya</s>) for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And that which is pure morality for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — that same [conduct] is impure morality and the height of immorality for one following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>. For what reason? Here, <s>Upāli</s>, one following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> does not accept rebirth (<s>bhavopapatti</s>) even for a single moment's thought. This is the pure morality for one following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>; that same [conduct] is impure morality and the height of immorality for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. What, <s>Upāli</s>, is the pure morality for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — that which is impure morality and the height of immorality for one following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>? Here, <s>Upāli</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> accepts rebirth for immeasurable, incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) with an unwearied mind and an untroubled heart. This is the pure morality for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; that same [conduct] is impure morality and the height of immorality for one following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>."

body.text: tasmāttarhi tvamupāle sānurakṣāṃ śikṣāṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ vada / niranurakṣāṃ śikṣāṃ śrāvakayānikānāṃ vada / saparihārāṃ śikṣāṃ mahāyānasamprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ vada / niḥparihārāṃ śikṣāṃ śrāvakayānikānāṃ vada / dūrānupraviṣṭāṃ śikṣāṃ mahāyānasamprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ vada / sāvadānāṃ śikṣāṃ śrāvakayānikānāṃ vada /
body.translated_text: "Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, speak of a training with precautionary safeguards (<s>sānurakṣā śikṣā</s>) for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; speak of a training without precautionary safeguards (<s>niranurakṣā śikṣā</s>) for those following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>. Speak of a training with concessions for offenses (<s>saparihārā śikṣā</s>) for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; speak of a training without concessions (<s>niḥparihārā śikṣā</s>) for those following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>. Speak of a training penetrating deeply (<s>dūrānupraviṣṭā śikṣā</s>) for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; speak of a training requiring careful vigilance (<s>sāvadānā śikṣā</s>) for those following the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>."

body.text: kathaṃ copāle sānurakṣā śikṣā mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ niranurakṣā śikṣā śrāvaka yānikānām / ihopāle mahāyāna saṃprasthitena bodhisattvena parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ hitamanuvartitavyaṃ na punaḥ śrāvakayānikena / anenopāle paryyāyeṇa sānurakṣā śikṣā mahāyānikānām bodhisattvānāṃ niranurakṣā śikṣā śrāvakayānikānām /
body.translated_text: And how, O <s>Upāli</s>, is the training of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) one with guarding, while the training of those of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Hearers' Vehicle) is without guarding? Here, O <s>Upāli</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> should pursue the welfare of other beings and other individuals, but one of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> need not. By this method, O <s>Upāli</s>, the training of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is with guarding, while the training of those of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> is without guarding.

body.text: kathaṃ copāle saparihārā śikṣā mahāyānasamprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ niḥ parihārāśikṣā śrāvakayānikānām / ihopāle mahānasaṃprasthitobodhisattvo 'pi saceta pūrvvāṇhasamaye āpattimāpadyeta madhyānhakāle sarvvajñatācittenāvirahito viharedaparyyantaḥ / evaṃ mahāyānasamprasthitasya bodhisattvasya śīlaskandha / sacenmadhyānhasamaye āpattimāpadyate sāyānhakāle sarvvajñatācittenāvirahito viharedaparyyantaḥ / evaṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitasya bodhisattvasya śīlaskandhaḥ / sacet sāyānhasamaey āpattimāpadyeta rātryāḥ purimayāme sarvvajñatācittenāvirahito viharedaparyyantaḥ / evaṃ mahāyānasaṃpratisthatasya bodhisattvasyaśīlaskandhaḥ / sacet rātryāḥ purimayāme āpattimāpadyeta rātryāśca madhyamayāme sarvvajñatācittenāvirahito viharedaparyyantaḥ / evaṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitasya bodhisattvasya śīlaskandhaḥ / sacet rātryā madhyamayāme āpattimāpadyeta rātryāśca paścimayāme sarvvajñatācittenāvirahito viharedaparyyantaḥ / evaṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitasya bodhisattvasya śīlaskandho veditavyaḥ / evaṃ hyupāle saparihārā śikṣā mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ / tatra bodhisattvena nātra kaukṛtyaparyyutthānamutpādyaṃ nātivipratisāriṇā bhavitavyaṃ / tatropāle sacecchrāvakayānikaḥ punaḥ punarāpattimāpadyeta naṣṭaḥ śrāvakayānikasya śīlaskandho veditavyaḥ / tat kasmāddhetoḥ / ādīpta śiraścailopamena hi śrāvakayānikena bhavitavyaṃ sarvakleśaprahāṇāya / evaṃ niḥparihārā śikṣā śrāvakayānikasya hyupāle parinirvvāṇakāmasya /
body.translated_text: And how, O <s>Upāli</s>, is the training of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> one with remedy, while the training of those of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> is without remedy? Here, O <s>Upāli</s>, even if a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> commits a transgression in the forenoon, if during midday he dwells without being separated from the mind of omniscience, then (his) <s>śīlaskandha</s> (aggregate of moral discipline) as a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is unlimited. If he commits a transgression at midday, and during the afternoon he dwells without being separated from the mind of omniscience, then (his) <s>śīlaskandha</s> as a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is unlimited. If he commits a transgression in the afternoon, and during the first watch of the night he dwells without being separated from the mind of omniscience, then (his) <s>śīlaskandha</s> as a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is unlimited. If he commits a transgression during the first watch of the night, and during the middle watch of the night he dwells without being separated from the mind of omniscience, then (his) <s>śīlaskandha</s> as a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is unlimited. If he commits a transgression during the middle watch of the night, and during the last watch of the night he dwells without being separated from the mind of omniscience, then (his) <s>śīlaskandha</s> as a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> should be known as unlimited. Thus, O <s>Upāli</s>, the training of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is with remedy. Therein, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should not give rise to an obsession with remorse, nor should he be excessively regretful. But, O <s>Upāli</s>, if one of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> commits transgressions again and again, the <s>śīlaskandha</s> (aggregate of moral discipline) of one of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> should be known as destroyed. Why is that? Because one of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> must be as if his head and clothes were on fire, striving for the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Thus, O <s>Upāli</s>, the training of one of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> who desires <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) is without remedy.

body.text: katham copāle dūrānupraviṣṭā śikṣā mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvnāṃ sāvadānā śikṣā śrāvakayānikānāṃ / ihopāle mahāyānasaṃprasthito bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālikāsamān kalpān pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ krīḍitvā ramitvā paricārayitvā bodhicittaṃ notsṛjati / ayamupāle mahāyānasaṃprasthitasya bodhisattvasya śikṣā veditavyā / tat kasmāddhetoḥ / bhaviṣyatyupāle sa kālaḥ sa samayo yanmahāyānasaṃprasthito bodhisattvastenaiva bodhicittena suparigṛhītena svapnāntaragato 'pi sarvvakleśairnna saṃhariṣyate / api ca mahāyānasaṃprasthitena bodhisattvena naikasminneva bhave sarvvakleśāḥ kṣapayitavyāḥ / anupūrvveṇa bodhisattvnāṃ kleśāḥ kṣayaṃ gacchantiḥ / paripakvakuśalamūlena ca śrāvakayānikenādīptaśi śacailopamena hi tatkṣaṇikokapi bhavopapattirnnotpāditavyā / evamupāle dūrānupraviṣṭā śikṣā mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sāvadānāṃ śikṣā śrāvakayānikānām //
body.translated_text: And how, O <s>Upāli</s>, is the training of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> one that has entered far (into the path), while the training of those of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> is one requiring vigilance? Here, O <s>Upāli</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, even after sporting, enjoying, and indulging in the five strands of sensual pleasure for <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) equal to the grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, does not abandon <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). This, O <s>Upāli</s>, should be known as the training of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Why is that? Because, O <s>Upāli</s>, there will come a time, there will come a moment, when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, well-protected by that very <s>bodhicitta</s>, will not be overcome by any <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), even when he has entered into a dream. Moreover, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> need not exhaust all <s>kleśas</s> in a single existence; gradually, the <s>kleśas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> go to exhaustion. But one of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> whose roots of merit are fully ripened, being as if his head and clothes were on fire, should not produce even a momentary rebirth in existence. Thus, O <s>Upāli</s>, the training of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> has entered far (into the path), while the training of those of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> requires vigilance.

body.text: tasmāttarhi tvamupāle sānurakṣāṃ saparihārāṃ dūrānupraviṣṭāṃ śikṣāṃ mahāyānasamprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ vada / niranurakṣāṃ niḥparihārām sāvadānāṃ śikṣāṃ śrāvakayānikānāṃ vada / tat kasmāddhetoḥ / mahāsaṃbhārā hyupāle 'nuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirna sukarā ekāntaniviṣṭena mahāyānasaṃprasthitena bodhisattvenā prameyāsaṃkhyeyān kalpān saṃdhārayituṃ saṃsarituma / idaṃ copāle 'rthavaśaṃ sampaśyan tathāgataḥ samyaksambuddho mahāyānāsaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvnāṃ naikāntanirvvedakathāṃ kathayati naikāntavirāgakathāṃ kathayati naikāntavirāgakathāṃ kathayati naikāntasaṃvegakathāṃkathaṃyati / api tu khalu punaḥ prītikathāṃ prāmodyakathām pratityasamutpādasamprayuktakathāṃ kathayati / gambhīrāmasaṃkliṣṭāṃ sūkṣmāṃ niḥkaukṛtyakathāṃ kathayati / niḥparyyutthānakathāṃ kathayati / asaṅgāmanāvaraṇāṃ śūnyatākathāṃ kathayati / ta imāṃ kathāṃ śrutvā 'bhiratāḥ saṃprāptā na parikhidyante bodhisambhārañca paripūrayanti /
body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, teach the training that is carefully guarded, well-protected, and deeply entered into for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). Teach the training that is unguarded, unprotected, yet cautious for those of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Hearers' Vehicle). For what reason? Because, <s>Upāli</s>, unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) requires great accumulations and is not easy — a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> must sustain and transmigrate through immeasurable, incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). And, <s>Upāli</s>, seeing this purpose, the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), the Perfectly Awakened One, does not teach <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> exclusively discourse on disgust, nor exclusively discourse on dispassion, nor exclusively discourse on urgency. Rather, he teaches discourse on joy, discourse on gladness, discourse connected with <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). He teaches discourse that is profound, undefiled, subtle, and free from remorse. He teaches discourse free from secondary afflictions. He teaches discourse on <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) that is unattached and unobstructed. Having heard this discourse, they remain delighted and content, do not become weary, and fulfill the accumulation of awakening.

body.text: atha hyāyuṣmānupāliḥ bhagavantametadavocat / yā imā bhagavannāpattayaḥ kāścidrāgasaṃyuktāḥ kāścit dveṣāsaṃyuktāḥ kāścinmohasaṃyuktāḥ / tatra katamā bhagavan mahāyānasaṃprasthitasya bodhisattvasya gurutarā āpattayaḥ / kiṃ rāgasaṃprayuktā utāho dveṣasaṃprayuktāḥ utāho mohasaṃprayuktāḥ / evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamupālimetadavocat / sacedupāle mahāyānasaṃprasthito bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā rāgasaṃprayuktā āpattīrāpadyeta yāñcaikāṃ dveṣasaṃprayuktāmāpattimāpadyeta bodhisattvayānaṃ pramāṇīkṛtyeya tābhyo gurutarā āpattiryeyam dveṣaprayuktā / tat kasmāddhetordveṣa upāle sattvaparityāgāya saṃvarttate rāgaḥ sattvasaṃgrahāya saṃvarttate iti / tatropāle yaḥ kleśaḥ sattvasaṃgrahāya saṃvarttate tatra bodhisattvasya na chalaṃ na bhayam / yaḥ kleśaḥ sattvaparityāgāya saṃvarttate tatra bodhisattvasya chalañca bhayañca / api tūpāle uktam pūrvvameva rāgo bandhavirāgo 'lpasāvadyo dveṣah kṣipravirāgo mahāsāvadyaḥ / tatropāle yo bandhavirāgokalpasāvadyaḥ saṃkleśaḥ............... bodhisattvasya / yaḥ kṣipravirāgo mahāsāvadyaḥ kleśaḥ sa bodhisattvasya svapnāntaragatasyāpi naiva yuktaḥ / tasmāttarhi tvamupāle bodhisattvānaṃ yāḥ kāścid rāgasaṃprayuktā āpattayaḥ sarvvāstā anāpattaya iti dhāraya / tatropāle ye 'nupāyakuśalā bodhisattvāste rāgasaṃprayuktābhya āpatibhyo vibhyati na dveṣasamprayuktābhyaḥ / ye punarupāyakuśalā bodhisattvāste dveṣasaṃprayuktābhya āpattibhyo vibhyati na rāgasamprayuktābhyaḥ / atha khalu te tasyāmeva parṣadi mañjuśrīkumarabhūtaḥ sannipatito 'bhūt / sa niṣaṇṇaḥ bhagavantametadavocat / atyantavinītānāṃ bhagavan sarvvadharmāṇāṃbodhāya vinayaḥ / evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat / sacenmañjuśrīrbbāla pṛthagjanā / ātyantavinītān sarvvadharmān jānīyustadapi na bhūyastathāgato vinayaḥ prajñāpyeta / sattvā na prīṇanti tasmāt tathāgato 'tyantavinītānāṃ sarvvadharmmānāṃ bodhāya vinayaṃ prajñāpayatyanupūrveṇeti yoniśamupādāya // 0 //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Upāli</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One): "<s>Bhagavān</s>, among these transgressions (<s>āpatti</s>), some are connected with passion (<s>rāga</s>), some with hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and some with delusion (<s>moha</s>). Among these, <s>Bhagavān</s>, which transgressions are more serious for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — those connected with passion, or those connected with hatred, or those connected with delusion?" Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Upāli</s>: "<s>Upāli</s>, even if a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> were to commit transgressions connected with passion equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, yet a single transgression connected with hatred — taking the <s>Bodhisattvayāna</s> (Bodhisattva Vehicle) as the standard — would be more serious than those connected with passion. For what reason? Because hatred, <s>Upāli</s>, leads to the abandonment of beings, while passion leads to the gathering of beings. Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, whichever <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) leads to the gathering of beings, in that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> need have neither deceit nor fear. But whichever <s>kleśa</s> leads to the abandonment of beings, in that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should have both deceit and fear. Moreover, <s>Upāli</s>, it has been said before: passion is slow to fade and of small fault; hatred is quick to fade but of great fault. Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, the defilement that is slow to fade and of small fault ... [is tolerable] for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. But the <s>kleśa</s> that is quick to fade and of great fault is not fitting for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> even in a dream. Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, hold that all transgressions connected with passion for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are as if they are non-transgressions. <s>Upāli</s>, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are unskilled in means fear transgressions connected with passion but not those connected with hatred. But those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are skilled in means fear transgressions connected with hatred but not those connected with passion." Then, in that very assembly, <s>Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta</s> (Prince Mañjuśrī) had assembled. Seated, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "<s>Bhagavān</s>, for all <s>dharmas</s> that are ultimately disciplined, discipline is for the sake of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>)." Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to <s>Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta</s>: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, if foolish ordinary persons (<s>bāla pṛthagjana</s>) were to know all <s>dharmas</s> as ultimately disciplined, then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would not further establish discipline. But beings are not satisfied; therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> establishes discipline for the sake of awakening of all <s>dharmas</s> that are ultimately disciplined, gradually, proceeding from proper attention."
